caption:
Calf cramp mid-run again? It's not always about salt.

Dehydration and electrolytes often get the blame, but research suggests muscle fatigue plays a big role. Cramps tend to hit late in a session, or when you go harder or longer than usual.

On the spot, stop and gently lengthen the muscle: pull your toes towards you and hold. Most cramps ease within a minute or two. If the same muscle keeps cramping, strengthening it with calf raises two or three times a week can help it cope. Build distance gradually.

See your GP if cramps happen often at rest, or come with calf swelling, redness or warmth. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help with the training side. Book online via the link in bio.
